parts.heading: Understanding Reparenting
parts.job: Opens the guide: defines reparenting as building an Inner Adult (Nurturer, Protector, Guide) who relates to the little one, names the chicken-and-egg problem and borrowed adulthood, lays out the five stages, and gives the author's own story.

parts.heading: Safety and Readiness
parts.job: Before any practice: checks the reader is grounded enough to go in, covers body-first work, what to do if therapy stirs things up, readers who would harm the child, and suicidal crisis.

parts.heading: Building Your Inner Adult
parts.job: The core of the guide: how to borrow and build the three Inner Adult roles (Protector, Nurturer, Guide) one competency at a time, including how to avoid outer gurus and manipulators.

parts.heading: Practicing With Your Little One
parts.job: The hands-on session methods: how to make contact (photos, other-hand journaling, no inner monologue needed), catch hooks, meditate, do a daily intention and review, and close the session.

parts.heading: Discovering and Healing Old Patterns
parts.job: Works with the old patterns from childhood: how distrust and shame reproduce, forgiveness, redoing memories of discipline or trauma with hindsight, and answering the inner strict disciplinarian.

parts.heading: When the Practice Gets Difficult
parts.job: Troubleshooting: when the adult voice feels fake, no clear child exists, practice stays shallow or turns into checking, how to tell if it helps, when to change strategy, urges to escape, and physical pain.

parts.heading: Altered States and Intensive Practice
parts.job: Guidance on using meditation retreats and psychedelics with the work: sober first, how to handle peaks, safety cautions (psychosis, medications, mixing), the author's own mistakes, and spiritual attack met with love.

parts.heading: Bringing Reparenting Into Real Life
parts.job: Takes the work out of sessions into life with other people: play and preferences, differentiation from belonging bargains, finding and trusting people, conflict, endings, and finding therapists.

parts.heading: Conclusion and Appendix
parts.job: Closes with reassurance of worth and Divine Love, then the appendix compares the guide to Capacchione's inner child therapy, Schema Therapy and IFS, and credits teachers.

roles.name: The Protector (safe Adult Protector); section: Protecting and Building Trust With Your Little One
roles.work: Keeps the little one safe through plain acts before warmth exists: sets boundaries, keeps one small promise, repairs after internal attacks, protects them from the inherited critical parent, and earns trust day to day like rent showing up each month. First safety in the child's order of receptivity. Introduced as a named role in N001, its section has no heading called 'Protector'.

roles.name: The Nurturer
roles.work: Loves the little one, even before it is trusted: says 'I believe you. And I love you', borrows love from others, from love for someone else, from goodwill or gratitude (divine love), invites the little one in, makes a simple vow, and shows up when nothing is wrong. Second in the child's order: feeling loved on top of safety.

roles.name: The Inner Guide: Becoming Your Own Shepherd
roles.work: Chooses what the little one learns and experiences and holds standards without the harsh inherited tone: borrows hindsight and past successes, accepts that a healthy mind is not a perfect mind, points to belonging beyond people, respects timing (needs enough Nurturer and Protector first), and steers between spoiling and clamping down. Third in the child's order: guidance once safety and love are in place. Added to the framework by Key.

notes: The guide's spine is one idea: the reader builds an Inner Adult made of three jobs done by one grown-up (Protector, Nurturer, Guide) toward the little one (the inner child), mostly by 'borrowing adulthood' (from people, memories, figures, spiritual sources, or a therapist) one small competency at a time, since the child will not heal itself ('forced adulthood'). The child's receptivity runs safety (Protector), then love (Nurturer), then guidance (Guide), and the three are developed alongside each other. Order of the whole: define and motivate (N001), readiness and safety (N005), build the roles (N015), practice methods (N052), heal old patterns (N067), troubleshoot (N076), altered states (N090), real life and other people (N105), close and appendix (N141). Recurring cast and terms: the little one; the Inner Adult; the inherited parent or Critic (the harsh script, the target of reframing and of 'Answering the Strict Disciplinarian'); protective parts or guards (anxiety, urge to escape, the 'nope') to be heard out rather than fought; hooks (Pema Chodron's shenpa); borrowed adulthood; forced adulthood; pl/ork (play plus work); the belonging bargains and differentiation; the food-bank/starving-baby image (spirituality without reparenting). Five stages (N003) are listed but have no headings. Spiritual material (loving-kindness, gratitude as Divine Love, Buddhist views) runs through the guide and is explicitly layered after safety and Nurturer/Protector (N050, N091). Several sections cross-refer by name (e.g. Borrow Hindsight, Noticing Counts, Timing Is Individual, Your Loan is PRE-APPROVED!, Untangling the Belonging Bargains, Altered States Can Deepen Therapy or Escapism). Heading levels are uneven: N105 holds text and sits as a level-1 part though it is also an intro to its own sub-sections; N005, N015, N052, N067, N076, N090 and N141 have no text of their own. Level 2 and 3 headings mix full sections with short 'if you...' branches (e.g. N057 to N061, N094 to N100, N084 to N086). Several sections sit in safety or hazard branches (N010 to N014, N093 to N100) and some personal-story sections (N004, N101, N102, N114) show the author's own path. The appendix compares to Schema Therapy and IFS by mapping their terms to the three roles.
